title: Beyond Binary Audits: Does Guideline Grounding Mitigate Decision-Space Framing in LLM Opioid Prescribing?
abstract: arXiv:2611.18631v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Audits of LLMs for bias in opioid prescribing have largely relied on binary treatment decisions, a signal that current models have saturated. We introduce Q-Pain++, a full-factorial stress test that holds clinical content fixed while independently varying clinical risk factors and the granularity of the available dosage options. Adding an intermediate dosage option to otherwise unchanged vignettes substantially lowers agreement with expert-annotated dosages for most models, while demographic differences in dosage decisions remain small in all but one configuration once clinical risk factors are added. Grounding models in perioperative guidelines through retrieval reduces this framing effect on average but does not eliminate it, and one model's treatment decisions change when the retrieved passages are reordered. These results suggest that audits should vary the answer format, not only patient identity. We will release our codebase as wel

translated_title: 超越二元审计：指南锚定能否缓解LLM阿片类药物处方中的决策空间框架效应？
translated_abstract: 针对LLM阿片类药物处方偏见的审计在很大程度上依赖于二元治疗决策，这一信号在当前模型上已趋于饱和。我们提出了Q-Pain++，这是一个全因子压力测试，在保持临床内容不变的前提下，独立变化临床风险因素和可用剂量选项的粒度。在其余内容不变的病例描述中增加一个中间剂量选项，会显著降低大多数模型与专家标注剂量的一致性，而在加入临床风险因素后，除一种配置外，剂量决策中的人口统计学差异在所有配置中都保持很小。通过检索将模型锚定于围手术期指南，平均而言可以减少这种框架效应但无法消除它，并且当检索到的段落重新排序时，一个模型的治疗决策会发生变化。这些结果表明，偏见审计应该变化答案格式，而不仅仅是变化患者身份。我们将发布我们的代码库等相关资源。
tldr: 论文提出Q-Pain++全因子压力测试，发现改变剂量选项的粒度会显著影响LLM的阿片类药物处方决策，而检索指南锚定虽能部分缓解但不能消除这种决策空间框架效应，表明偏见审计应变化答案格式而不仅是患者身份。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces Q-Pain++, a full-factorial stress test showing that varying dosage option granularity substantially shifts LLM opioid prescribing decisions, and that grounding in guidelines via retrieval mitigates but does not eliminate this framing effect, suggesting audits should vary answer formats beyond patient identity.
